what_this_is: Four agents, working independently and read-only, re-ran the author's claims before this package was handed over. They were told to find anything false, overstated or unverifiable, and that a claim which reproduces is as useful a finding as one that does not. This file is their raw output, including every disagreement with the author.

reports.summary: I re-ran all five claims on the clean worktree at HEAD 86ba3d75431c56147f229f24794805a3d8504f76 (branch research/helm-3.0-cas-lab, `git status --porcelain` empty, so every number below comes from committed state). All five reproduce exactly: 458, 348, 48/48, 39/39, and the 99-test file byte-identical. No claim was false. I found four things the package should say but does not, and they are all about framing rather than arithmetic. (1) The stated list of 2026-09-21 commits is incomplete — at least seven more commits carry that date, including a32d05c8 (15:28) and c3855275 (15:30) on this same line, and c3855275 is the very baseline claim 5 diffs against. (2) "458 compiler tests" is literally what pytest prints, but 359 of the 458 come from four test files that did not exist at the baseline, and 270 of the 458 are three parametrized functions run over 90 help-text examples in one file; only 99 pre-date the work. An auditor reading "458 tests pass" as 458 independent compiler behaviours would be misled. (3) The "48/48" headline for cas_ohm comes from a commit that wrote its own nine new tests. I checked whether those tests are real by running HEAD's test file against the pre-change quantifiers.py: six of them fail there by name, so the fix is genuine and not self-confirming — but that check is mine, not the package's, and should be included. (4) The codex worktree named in the context has moved on; it is now at 5b3d713c on branch codex/helm-cas-rpa-atlas-20260922, not at 04547c55, so an auditor who goes there today will not find the merged state. I also spot-checked the self-correction commit f46d34cb and the 58/42 recount it asserts; both hold under independent measurement. No command I ran errored. Every command's exit code was 0 except the deliberate old-code-versus-new-tests run, which exited 1 as designed.

reports.anything_else_wrong:
Five things, none of which makes a stated number wrong.

1. The list of 2026-09-21 commits is incomplete. The package names eight: 7f32129d, 8febba71, dbb388ee, 0fc6bb30, d50abbbc, 078d00ed, f46d34cb, 86ba3d75. `git log --format="%h %ad %s" --date=format:"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"` shows at least seven more with that same date: a32d05c8 (15:28), c3855275 (15:30), 0c4eb7da (19:37), 8feed0cf (20:14), 8c409a28 (20:13), a5956609 (20:16), 5f6c1231 (20:27), plus 04547c55 (20:31) which the context mentions only as the merged codex tip. This matters because c3855275 is the baseline claim 5 diffs against. An auditor handed the eight-commit list and then told to diff from c3855275 has no way to see where that commit sits.

2. The codex worktree pointer is stale. The context says a second agent's worktree is at .../\_worktrees/codex-helm-data. It exists, but it is now at HEAD 5b3d713c5e7f2b2fc2959aaf776d0d80ca09d256 on branch codex/helm-cas-rpa-atlas-20260922 — not 04547c55, not codex/helm-cas-data-boundary-20260921. An auditor who goes there expecting the merged state will find newer work. Give them the commit hash 04547c55 instead of the directory path.

3. "About 3 minutes" for the lab suite is low. It took 292.05 seconds (4 minutes 52 seconds). Small, but the audit brief tells people to notice errored or truncated commands, and a run that looks 60% over its stated budget invites someone to kill it and call it hung.

4. The 458 number needs one sentence of context or it overstates. Literally it is right and I reproduced it twice. But 99 of the 458 pre-date the work and 359 do not, and 270 of the 458 come from three parametrized test functions run over 90 help-text example rows in a single file (test_offline_help_text_canon.py: six def test_ functions, 273 collected tests). The suite is real and it passes; it is just not 458 independent compiler behaviours. Say so before someone else says it for you.

5. The 48/48 claim should ship with the falsification check, not just the count. On its own, "39/39 -> 48/48" from a commit that wrote its own nine tests proves nothing. I ran HEAD's test_quantifiers.py against 078d00ed's quantifiers.py and got "PASSED 42/48" with six tests failing by name (i_pred returned inf / 0.0 / nan, r_total returned inf / nan). That is the evidence that makes 48/48 mean something, and it is reproducible in about two commands. Include it.

Two claims outside my assigned five, which I checked because they are corrections of earlier wrong claims and corrections are worth verifying. Both hold. Commit f46d34cb asserts that at pre-edit tree dbb388ee, Chapter_10_Special_Purpose_Components.md line 278 already read `gate dissonance: XOR< attract, averse >;` — it does, verbatim, including the trailing comment "// fires -> genuine conflict" — and that Appendix_E_Exercise_Answers.md line 327 used the xor prefix for the same declaration — it reads `    xor dissonance: XOR< attract, averse >;`. At HEAD both now read `gate conflict: AND< attract, averse >;` (Chapter_10 line 281, Appendix_E line 327) and a scan of all 40 PCBA markdown files at HEAD found zero remaining occurrences of "gate dissonance". The same commit asserts a recount of 58 listing blocks across 42 distinct names; I counted independently with my own script over `HEAD:book/CAS_PCBA_Engineer/*.md`, matching lines of the form `circuit|board <name> {`, and got TOTAL 58, DISTINCT 42. Exact match.

Process notes for the auditor. The worktree was clean throughout — `git status --porcelain` returned nothing — so every number came from committed state, not from uncommitted edits. I made no changes to any file under tksCAS; the pre-change and mixed-version runs were done on copies in the session scratchpad. No command I ran errored or was truncated. Exit codes were 0 for claims 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, and 1 for the deliberate old-code-versus-new-tests run, which is the expected failure.

reports.summary:
I re-ran every claim from my own scratch folder. Nothing under tksCAS was written to. The arithmetic claims hold up exactly. The story told about them does not.

WHAT HOLDS: all five bad values reproduce exactly in the BEFORE code (blob 2c98a773, commit 078d00ed). All five are refused in the AFTER code (blob 11b6dbd9, commit 86ba3d75) with a ValueError whose message contains the word "finite". Every "unchanged" value is unchanged. The test counts are right: 39 passed before, 48 passed after, and the diff adds exactly nine test functions. The cited origin commit 3ea9dbe6 exists and added exactly 1,470 lines.

WHAT DOES NOT HOLD: my strongest claim is wrong. I said i_pred(8.0, inf) -> 0.0 "reads downstream as a starved path", and the CHANGELOG goes further and calls it "an ASOM classification produced from garbage". No such code path exists. asom() takes two enums and never reads a flow number. STARVED comes only from asom(Region.CUTOFF, Outcome.INTENDED), and Region is always handed in by the caller. No function in the module returns a Region. I fed the bad 0.0 into the one function that does consume a flow number, delta_current, and got sign=OVERSHOOT -- the opposite direction from starved.

Worse for my claim: I picked the wrong value as the dangerous one. Feeding the two NaN cases into delta_current gives sign=WITHIN_TOLERANCE, the same reading a correct prediction gives. Those are the quiet failures. The 0.0 is loud.

Two smaller errors: "NaN compares False against every operator" is false as written (nan != 0.0 is True), and "No test covered a non-finite input" is false (test_r_hidden_censors_non_finite already passed nan and inf to r_hidden).

And one defect survives the fix: r_hidden(v=nan, i_obs=2.0, r_known=2.0) still returns RHidden(magnitude=nan) at HEAD.

checks.claim: Cause: NaN passes that guard because NaN compares False against every operator
checks.how_i_checked: `python -c` evaluating nan against each comparison operator.
checks.observed: nan < 0.0 -> False ; nan <= 0.0 -> False ; nan > 0.0 -> False ; nan >= 0.0 -> False ; nan == 0.0 -> False ; nan != 0.0 -> True
checks.note: The conclusion is right and the mechanism is right: `nan <= 0.0` is False, so NaN slides through the strictly-positive test. But "every operator" is false as written. `nan != 0.0` returns True. The accurate sentence is: NaN compares False against every ORDERING and EQUALITY operator, and True against !=. An auditor can falsify the literal sentence in one line, so it should be corrected before the package goes out.

checks.claim: Cause: the module already contained a _is_finite helper that _as_resistance did not call
checks.how_i_checked: `grep -n "_is_finite\|_as_resistance" scratchpad/before/cas_ohm/quantifiers.py`, then read both regions with sed.
checks.observed: In the before file, `def _as_resistance` is at line 198 and its body (lines 198-213) contains no call to _is_finite. `def _is_finite` is at line 540. The diff confirms the fix moved the helper from line 540 to just above _as_resistance.
checks.note: Accurate. One nuance for the auditor: the CHANGELOG says `_is_finite` was "hoisted above its first use", which implies the old ordering was a problem. It was not. In the before code, r_hidden called _is_finite at lines 490, 516 and 527 -- all ABOVE the line-540 definition -- and that worked, because Python resolves module-level names at call time, not at definition time. The hoist is cosmetic tidying, not part of the fix.

checks.claim: STRONGEST CLAIM: i_pred(8.0, inf) -> 0.0 is "the dangerous one" because a zero flow "reads downstream as a starved path" -- and in the CHANGELOG, "an ASOM classification produced from garbage"
checks.how_i_checked: Wrote scratchpad/starved_probe.py and ran it against scratchpad/before, where i_pred(8.0, inf) really does return 0.0. It (a) reads asom's signature, (b) tries passing the 0.0 straight to asom, (c) enumerates asom over all 7 Region values, (d) uses inspect to search every module-level function for one annotated to return a Region, (e) feeds the bad 0.0 into delta_current, the only function in the module that consumes a flow number. I also ran `grep -n "Region.CUTOFF\|-> Region"` over the after file.
checks.observed: asom signature: `(region: 'Region', outcome: 'Outcome') -> 'Optional[AsomLabel]'`. Passing the number directly: `asom(0.0, INTENDED) -> None` -- not STARVED. STARVED appears only at `asom(CUTOFF, INTENDED) -> AsomLabel.STARVED`. Functions annotated -> Region: `NONE`. `Region.CUTOFF` occurs exactly once outside the enum, at line 762, inside asom itself, comparing an already-supplied enum. Region reaches every consumer as a caller-supplied parameter: `delta_current(..., region: 'Region' = <Region.ACTIVE: 'ACTIVE'>)`, `asom(region, outcome)`, `check_eligibility(region, ...)`. Feeding the bad value to the real numeric consumer: `delta_current(i_obs=2.0, i_pred_value=0.0) -> value=2.0 sign=OVERSHOOT region=ACTIVE`. And delta_current refuses the CUTOFF region outright: `RAISED EligibilityError: delta_current refuses to run in region CUTOFF: a residual is admissible ONLY in the ACTIVE region (ch06:63-68)`.
checks.note: OVERSTATED for the commit-message wording and FALSE for the CHANGELOG wording. There is no code path from a flow number to AsomLabel.STARVED. The 0.0 in fact drives delta_current to OVERSHOOT -- the opposite direction from starved. The defensible version is narrower: a 0.0 is quieter than a NaN or an inf because it looks like a legitimate number, and it does corrupt the residual sign that the module says "ranks which follow-up PROBE to spend the next measurement budget on". reports.anything_else_wrong:
FIVE things the package should say and does not.

1. A DEFECT OF THE SAME CLASS SURVIVES AT HEAD. r_hidden never checks its drive argument v. Run: `r_hidden(v=nan, i_obs=2.0, r_known=2.0) -> RHidden magnitude=nan` and `r_hidden(v=inf, i_obs=2.0, r_known=2.0) -> RHidden magnitude=inf`. This is at commit 86ba3d75, blob 11b6dbd9, working tree clean (`git status --porcelain` on the cas_ohm folder returns nothing). i_pred got a drive check; r_hidden did not. The commit says the monograph rule is that an undefined quantity is "refused with a reason, never emitted" -- and HEAD still emits one. The fix is narrower than the principle it cites. An auditor will find this.

2. I PICKED THE WRONG VALUE AS THE DANGEROUS ONE. I fed all four bad i_pred values into delta_current, the module's only numeric consumer of a flow value. Results: 0.0 -> `value=2.0 sign=OVERSHOOT`; nan -> `value=nan sign=WITHIN_TOLERANCE` (both NaN cases); inf -> `value=-inf sign=UNDERSHOOT`; and a CORRECT prediction of 2.0 -> `value=0.0 sign=WITHIN_TOLERANCE`. The two NaN cases produce the SAME sign reading as a perfectly good prediction, because `nan < -tol` and `nan > tol` are both False and the code falls through to WITHIN_TOLERANCE, whose own docstring calls it "residual is zero-compatible". That is the silent failure. The 0.0 produces OVERSHOOT, which is loud and visibly different. My "quiet one" argument points at the wrong row of the table.

3. A THIRD PUBLIC FUNCTION CHANGED BEHAVIOUR AND IS NOT REPORTED. r_hidden calls _as_resistance for r_known, so it inherited the new refusal. Before: `r_hidden(v=8,i_obs=2,r_known=nan) -> RHidden magnitude=nan` and `r_known=inf -> RHidden magnitude=-inf`. After: both raise ValueError. This is a good change, but the commit's "Fix:" paragraph names only _as_resistance, i_pred and r_total, and the "Unchanged and verified" paragraph does not mention it. A third function's public behaviour moved silently.

4. THE MODULE HAS NO DOWNSTREAM CONSUMER AT ALL. `grep -rn "from cas_ohm|import cas_ohm|from .quantifiers|api.cas_ohm" --include=*.py` over the whole worktree returns exactly two hits: the package's own __init__.py line 10 and its own test_quantifiers.py line 15. Nothing else in the repository imports it. So the word "downstream" in my claim has no referent in code today. The defect was real and worth fixing, but the harm was hypothetical, and the package should say so rather than describe a consequence chain that does not exist.

5. THE FIX USES TWO DIFFERENT POLICIES FOR THE SAME BAD INPUT. A non-finite i_obs into r_hidden is CENSORED (returns a CensoredResult with a written reason). A non-finite r_known or a non-finite drive into i_pred is REFUSED (raises). The commit gives a rationale -- "a caller error is not an observation, so it is not censored" -- which is coherent. But the package should state it as a deliberate split, because a reader comparing `r_hidden(i_obs=nan)` returning an object against `i_pred(v=nan)` raising will otherwise read it as an inconsistency.

reports.summary:
I re-ran every claim assigned to me. Eight of eleven sub-claims reproduce exactly; one reproduces with a caveat; one is overstated; one cannot be checked directly because the artifact no longer exists.

The strongest result: the canon pin holds. Commit d50abbbc and commit eb3c9b1e are byte-identical on all eight changed files — not merely identical after LF-normalising, but identical raw, before any normalising. All 40 book .md files match after LF-normalising. The two repositories really are separate (different git common directories). The book directory at d50abbbc is also unchanged at the branch tip 86ba3d75.

The defect claims hold. XOR really was called a both-active detector in the committed book. The self-correction is itself correct in every part I could test: Chapter_10 line 278 reads exactly 'gate dissonance: XOR< attract, averse >;' in the pre-edit tree, Chapter_14 really carries two gate statements, and the chapter and its answer key really did use different prefixes. The count of 58 blocks across 42 names is right; I also found where the earlier 60 came from.

Three things the auditor package should fix before it goes out.

One. The line-ending claim is overstated. It is true in the helm3-lab worktree. It is false in the main repository at tksCAS, where 24 of the book files sit CRLF in the working tree and one is mixed. The index is LF in both. The claim needs a repository scope or an auditor will mark it false.

Two. A line-number trap. The brief's "Appendix_B:374" refers to the edited working copy, not the committed book. In the committed pre-edit book, line 374 is the XOR line, not the NOT line. An auditor who opens 374 in the pre-edit tree will find a different line than the brief quotes and may wrongly call the claim false. The edited working copy no longer exists in any tree, so that one claim cannot be read back directly.

Three. The edits left two instances of the defect they were made to remove. The canon pin still calls the op-amp a CJT at Chapter_10 line 322 and Appendix_B line 65, while both op-amp sections were rewritten to stop doing exactly that.

Nothing I checked was fabricated. No command I ran errored. Every number below is quoted from output, not paraphrased.

reports.anything_else_wrong:
Three findings the package should carry, plus two smaller notes. None of these change the OD-A decision or the canon pin. All were found by reading the canon pin itself.

FINDING 1 — THE EDITS LEFT TWO INSTANCES OF THE DEFECT THEY WERE MADE TO REMOVE. This is the most important thing I found. The OD-A edits deliberately stopped calling the op-amp a CJT. Both section headings changed from "Op-Amp — Ultra-High-Gain CJT with Feedback" to "Op-Amp — High-Gain Differential Stage with Feedback", in Chapter_10 and in Appendix_B. Appendix_B's op-amp body changed from "It is a CJT with so much raw gain you tame it with feedback rather than relying on native beta" to "This is a differential construction, not a Noetic involution operator." But two sentences elsewhere were missed and survive in the canon pin d50abbbc:
  - Chapter_10_Special_Purpose_Components.md line 322, in the chapter's own summary bullets: "**Op-Amp** is an ultra-high-gain CJT tamed by feedback — set the *closed-loop* gain (`1 + Rf/Rg`), never run reasoning open-loop."
  - Appendix_B_Component_Datasheets.md line 65, in the CJT datasheet's Typical use section: "The op-amp is a CJT with so much raw gain it must be tamed by feedback."
Both are byte-identical to the pre-edit text; line 65 sits at line 63 in the pre-edit tree, shifted only by lines added above it. So the canon pin still contradicts itself on the same point the edits were made to settle. A third-party auditor will find these, and it is better that the package names them first. This is a follow-up defect, not a reason to unpin d50abbbc.

FINDING 2 — AN UNEXPLAINED 27-LINE GAP IN THE BRIEF'S CHANGELOG COUNT. The brief lists the pre-fix edit sizes and ends with "plus 70 new CHANGELOG lines". The measured diff from dbb388ee to d50abbbc for book/CAS_PCBA_Engineer/CHANGELOG.md is 97 insertions and 0 deletions. Every other file in that list matches exactly (Chapter_10 67, Appendix_C 23, Appendix_E 12, Chapter_15 2, Chapter_18 2), and Appendix_B differs by exactly the 2 lines of the owner's fix. So 97 against 70 is the one number in the list that does not reconcile. The likely innocent explanation is that CHANGELOG entries were added at commit time, after the brief was written. But the package should say so, because the auditor will check the arithmetic and this is the only line that does not close.

FINDING 3 — I CONFIRMED THE SWEEP IS OTHERWISE CLEAN. I searched every book .md file at the canon pin for leftovers of the same defect class. The phrase "dissonance detector" is gone from the book entirely: zero matches. No line still describes NOT as an involution flip: zero matches.
